title: JC H2 differentiation: connected rates of change
subject: math

slots.label: Rates that pull each other along
entries: Rates that pull each other along: as the radius of a circle grows, its area must grow too - the rate dA/dt is linked to the rate dr/dt by the relation between the quantities.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: The expanding circle
entries: The expanding circle: differentiating A = pi r^2 gives dA/dr = 2 pi r, the chain rule attaches dr/dt, and at r = 2 with dr/dt = 1/2 the substitution gives dA/dt = 2 pi, about 6.28 square units per second.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: The sliding ladder
entries: The sliding ladder: the fixed length gives x^2 + y^2 = 25 at every instant, and differentiating both sides with respect to time gives 2x dx/dt + 2y dy/dt = 0, because the constant 25 differentiates to 0.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: A common mistake
entries: A common mistake: cancelling the d's: dy/dx looks like a fraction, so its parts look separable - but it is one symbol for a limit, and pulling it apart breaks the mathematics.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: The connected-rates toolkit
entries: The connected-rates toolkit: write the relation, differentiate with respect to time, substitute the snapshot values, solve - the circle grew at 2 pi and the ladder top fell at 0.75 units per second from the same four steps.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Connected rates of change
entries: Rates of linked quantities: when a relation ties two quantities together, their rates of change are tied too, as the radius of a circle drags its area along.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Chain rule
entries: The rule that differentiates a quantity through a link: for A = pi r^2 changing with time, dA/dt = dA/dr x dr/dt = 2 pi r dr/dt.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Derivative
entries: The rate of change of one quantity with respect to another, defined as a limit: dy/dx is the limit of the average rate as the interval shrinks to zero.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Rate of change
entries: How fast a quantity changes per unit of time in these problems: dr/dt = 1/2 means the radius grows by half a unit every second.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Limit
entries: The value a quantity approaches as an interval shrinks toward zero: dy/dx is one symbol for this limit, which is why it cannot be pulled apart into pieces.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Snapshot values
entries: The values of the variables at the one instant asked about, such as x = 3 and y = 4 for the ladder: they are substituted only after the relation has been differentiated.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
